verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed mission of NASA's Artemis program.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'The Artemis II test flight will be NASA’s first mission with crew aboard'; R3: 'first crewed flight of the SLS rocket and Orion'; R4: 'first crewed launch of NASA’s SLS rocket'; R5: 'first crewed flight atop NASA's Space Launch System rocket'; R6: 'NASA's Artemis II crewed moon mission'; R7: 'first crewed launch of NASA’s SLS rocket'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state Artemis II as the first crewed mission in the program following uncrewed Artemis I.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is targeted for launch no earlier than Wednesday, April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'launch date for NASA’s Artemis II is either April 1 or April 2, 2026'; R4: 'targeting no earlier than Wednesday, April 1'; R6: 'scheduled to launch on Wednesday, April 1'; R7: 'targeted launch time of 6:24 p.m. on Wednesday, April 1'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly confirm the target launch date as no earlier than April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is targeted to launch from Kennedy Space Center's Pad 39B in Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Kennedy Space Center’s LC-39B'; R4: 'Launch Complex 39B... NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R6: 'Pad 39B at NASA's Kennedy Space Center'; R7: 'Launch Pad 39B'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly specify Pad 39B (LC-39B) at Kennedy Space Center, Florida.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is aimed at taking four astronauts on a 10-day flight around the moon and back.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R3: 'four astronauts... 10-day mission... orbit the Moon'; R6: 'Three NASA astronauts and a Canadian astronaut... 10-day flight'; R5: 'crew of four astronauts... nine-day trip around the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm four astronauts and flight around the moon, but duration is 10 days in R3/R6 vs. nine days in R5, creating contradiction.

verifications.claim: Artemis II follows the successful uncrewed Artemis I test flight.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Artemis II builds on the success of the uncrewed Artemis I in 2022'; R3: 'ahead of the uncrewed Artemis I launch'; R5: 'unpiloted Artemis I test flight in 2022'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state Artemis II follows successful uncrewed Artemis I.

verifications.claim: Artemis I test flight occurred in November 2022.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'blasted off on its debut flight... early on Wednesday' (Nov 2022 context); R2: 'uncrewed Artemis I in 2022'; R3: 'Nov. 4, 2022, ahead of the uncrewed Artemis I launch'; R5: 'Artemis I test flight in 2022'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm 2022 occurrence with November context (R1 launch report, R3 Nov 4 pre-launch), but no explicit 'November' statement.

verifications.claim: Artemis I test flight was uncrewed.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'three test dummies on board'; R2: 'uncrewed Artemis I'; R3: 'uncrewed Artemis I launch'; R5: 'unpiloted Artemis I test flight'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm Artemis I was uncrewed.

verifications.claim: Artemis I test flight was successful.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'blasted off... bringing the United States a big step closer' (successful launch report); R2: 'success of the uncrewed Artemis I'; R5: 'Orion capsule performed well' (despite heat shield notes, overall success)
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe Artemis I as successful, building block for Artemis II.

verifications.claim: Artemis I is the first in the series of moon missions.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The liftoff marked the start of NASA’s Artemis lunar exploration programme'; R3: 'second major flight of the Artemis campaign' (implying Artemis I first)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly position Artemis I as the start/first of the Artemis moon mission series.
